propositions: rebar MCP server emits nanosecond-precision timestamps (from time.time_ns()) as bare JSON numbers exceeding RFC 8259 §6 safe-integer range (±2^53-1), causing lossless-parsing JavaScript clients to receive BigInt values that cannot be stringified

GitHub Copilot CLI and other JS MCP clients parse JSON numbers outside the safe range as BigInt, then fail with 'TypeError: Do not know how to serialize a BigInt' when the client re-stringifies the tool result

Tools returning ticket records (list_tickets, ready_tickets, show_ticket, sign_manifest, verify_signature, plan_review_status) emit 2-144 unsafe integers per call; tools with no ticket timestamps (search, summary, ticket_deps) emit zero and do not fail
Plain JSON.parse silently truncates these values (1787856371950409998 becomes 1787856371950410000), causing data corruption in clients that do not preserve precision
The fix requires converting out-of-range integers to decimal strings at the MCP tool-return boundary only, preserving Python int semantics internally and in CLI/library surfaces
